title: Karan Johar to Make Film on R&AW Founder R.N. Kao, Sets August 2028 Release
excerpt: The Dharma Productions feature, based on Nitin Gokhale's 'Gentleman Spymaster,' will trace Kao's journey from 1955 to the 1971 war, timed to R&AW's 60th anniversary.
body:
• Dharma Productions and Leo Media Collective have announced a feature film on Rameshwar Nath Kao, the founder and first chief of India's external intelligence agency R&AW.
  • The film, based on Nitin Gokhale's book Gentleman Spymaster, is scheduled for worldwide theatrical release on August 11, 2028 — timed to mark R&AW's 60th anniversary.
  • The story will span 1955 to 1971, covering the circumstances that led to R&AW's creation in 1968 and its first mission during the 1971 war with Pakistan.
  • The project is currently in development; the director and cast have not been announced, though reports say an A-list actor will lead.

Karan Johar has announced a feature film on Rameshwar Nath Kao — the founding chief of India's external intelligence agency, the Research and Analysis Wing — with a theatrical release locked for August 11, 2028.

The announcement, made on September 21, was deliberately timed: the date marks 58 years since R&AW's founding, and the 2028 release — falling on the Independence Day weekend — is intended to honour the agency's 60th anniversary. The film will be produced by Johar's Dharma Productions in collaboration with Leo Media Collective, with Adar Poonawalla, Apoorva Mehta and Amritpal Singh Bindra among the associated team members.

The project

The film is based on Gentleman Spymaster, the book on Kao by former NDTV journalist Nitin Gokhale. According to the makers, it will trace the circumstances that led to the creation of R&AW, its formation in 1968, and its inaugural mission — the story spanning from 1955 to 1971 and culminating in the 1971 war with Pakistan.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=upBN-rPPVR4

The yet-untitled project is currently in development. Johar said Leo Media Collective has spent the past two years researching and dramatising the story, and the film is planned as a large-scale espionage-action feature expected to go on floors by mid-2026, according to reports. The director and cast remain under wraps, though insiders cited by entertainment media say an A-lister will spearhead the project.

"He built the invisible… but history remembers his impact."

— Karan Johar, announcing the film

"Leo Media has painstakingly been researching and dramatising this narrative with passion for the past two years," Johar said. "We want this film to be a gripping story based on true facts to pay homage to RAW and honour their milestone year with a solid motion picture … all of us at Dharma are so excited to get going."

Who was R.N. Kao?

For readers who did not grow up on stories of India's intelligence establishment, Rameshwar Nath Kao is one of the most consequential — and least publicly visible — figures in modern Indian history. A career intelligence officer, Kao headed the Intelligence Bureau's Aviation Research Centre and worked closely with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru before being handpicked to build India's external intelligence agency from scratch. He became the founding chief of R&AW when it was established in 1968.

Kao's tenure coincided with one of the defining conflicts of the subcontinent: the 1971 war with Pakistan, in which his agency's work was significant in the events leading to the emergence of Bangladesh. Within the world of espionage, he is regarded as the man who brought Indian intelligence craft to the global stage — a spymaster who operated almost entirely in the shadows.

A crowded lane for spy stories

The film lands in a genre Johar's banner has mined successfully in recent years. Dharma Productions has backed a string of fact-based patriotic dramas — Kesari, Raazi, Shershaah and Kesari: Chapter 2 — and the Kao film follows that template: an unsung national figure, a big-scale canvas, and a release date staked nearly two years out.

It is not the first screen project attempted around Kao. In 2022, filmmaker Hansal Mehta was announced as the creator and showrunner of an OTT series inspired by R.K. Yadav's book Mission R&AW, expected to chronicle Kao's journey as R&AW's first chief. No major public updates have followed since that announcement — which leaves Johar's film, with a confirmed theatrical date, as the furthest-advanced Kao project to date.

What's next

With the film still in development, the next milestones are the director announcement, the casting of the lead — the A-lister question will dominate trade chatter — and the start of production targeted for mid-2026. For now, the August 11, 2028 date gives the makers nearly two years to turn two years of research into a finished film.
nri_angle: R.N. Kao is a towering but little-known figure for many NRIs; the film could become the definitive mainstream introduction to the founder of India's external intelligence agency.
